completion_gate: All six declared artifacts exist and raw-result.json parses.
Every pre-registered control has a recorded pass/fail/void verdict.
The manifest records requested_policy, resolved model identifier, fallback_used, and degraded_requirements.
The execution report states a validity status with a reason, and states the exact ell range and sample sizes actually achieved.
constraints: Record observations only. Do not interpret results, do not compare to NIST margins beyond mechanically applying the contract's pre-registered extrapolation law, and do not change any hypothesis status.

If the frozen contract is underspecified on any point that changes the number, STOP and report the underspecification instead of choosing for yourself. An Executor that fills a gap in a frozen protocol has silently redesigned the experiment.

Count F_{p^2} multiplications exactly by instrumentation, not by timing. Wall-clock timings may be recorded alongside, but the reported cost unit is the counted multiplication, because that is the unit the paper's Section 4.1 estimate uses.

Run EVERY pre-registered control (C-NULL, C-INSTR, C-BASE, C-ALT). A measurement whose null-object control fails is void and must be reported as void - not repaired by adjusting the instrument until the null passes.

Modular polynomials must come from the provenance route the contract declares; record the URL, fetch timestamp, and SHA-256 of anything fetched, or the exact in-repo computation used. Never hardcode coefficients from memory - unverified recollection of Phi_ell coefficients is fabrication under AGENTS.md rule 9.

Preserve the full receipt: exact command, git commit and dirty-tree state, Python and dependency versions, all parameters and seeds, requested policy, resolved model identifier, fallback_used, degraded_requirements, stdout, stderr, raw machine-readable results, validity status with reason, timestamps, and resource measurements.

Respect the budget. If the ell grid cannot be completed, report the range actually reached and mark the run valid-but-truncated with the achieved scope; a truncated grid is scoped evidence. A timeout or crash is failed_infrastructure and is never evidence against the attack (AGENTS.md rule 5).
Every number in raw-result.json must be produced by code in this run. Do not carry forward a figure from EXP-P13VOW-001 or from the red-team report except as a labelled input constant.
deliverables: runs/RUN-PEC-6be870-a/ complete receipt bundle (manifest, raw-result, execution report, stdout, stderr)
inputs: inputs/P13-PANNY-POC/p-one-third.py (algorithmic reference; SageMath is NOT installed, so re-implement in pure Python and say so)
handoff.objective: Implement and run the frozen EXP-PEC-6be870 protocol exactly as specified: instrument Algorithm 1's table-construction step at p ~ 2^40 with an exact F_{p^2}-multiplication counter, measure per_entry(ell) over the pre-registered ell grid, run every pre-registered control, and report the fitted exponent gamma and the extrapolated c with their uncertainty.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether the paper's Section 4.1 assumption of one F_{p^2}-operation per table entry understates the true per-entry cost, and by an exponent of what size - the quantity that decides whether the NIST-I margin is ~34 bits (c = 0) or ~2 bits (c ~ 2).

dispatches.title: Execute NC-2: measure per-entry table-construction cost at p ~ 2^40 (EXP-PEC-6be870)

objective: GOAL-P13-001 BATCH-002 executes red-team next-control NC-2 (DEC-20260724-016), the single deciding measurement for the concrete NIST-I question left INCONCLUSIVE by BATCH-001: the true per-entry cost of Algorithm 1's table construction, which paper Section 4.1 assumes to be exactly one F_{p^2}-operation. The batch freezes an experiment contract (EXP-PEC-6be870) and the Panny proof-of-concept source named by NC-2, runs one bounded Executor measurement at p ~ 2^40 with pre-registered null-object and instrument-fidelity controls, and closes with independent Validator and Red Team review before a ledger archive. The batch measures a toy-scale exponent and states an explicit extrapolation law; it does not claim a cryptographic-scale result and does not by itself promote or reject H-P13-001.
